assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening a genuinely new observational window: a cubic-kilometre detector built in Antarctic ice that identified a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos in the TeV-PeV range, then pointed to sources. The detector concept and its calibration are a patient instrument achievement, which is the type of work I judge best. Lasting impact on multimessenger astronomy is clear.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and its predecessor AMANDA, and is the single credited name. A prize for the discovery would sit awkwardly with the very large collaboration and with other leading figures not in the supplied credit. One name is workable, but credit is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Diffuse flux confirmed by IceCube's own independent analyses and later source associations (TXS 0506+056 coincident flare, NGC 1068 evidence). Source identification is still limited in significance, but the discovery of the flux is stable. Recognition is timely, and KM3NeT results may add independent confirmation.
uncertainties: Credit rests on one named person while discovery was collaborative; other contributors are not in the supplied credit.
Individual source associations are still at 3-4 sigma level; I am relying on memory for these details, not on verification.
Independent confirmation by a second detector is only beginning.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological band theory introduced a new class of matter, with a prediction of the quantum spin Hall state, then 3D topological insulators, and it changed how materials are classified. The impact on condensed-matter physics is very large and has lasted two decades. This is outside my own field, so I rely on the committee's specialists to test the weighting.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposal. Molenkamp's group made the experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe wells (after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, who are not credited here). Hasan led the early ARPES work on 3D topological insulators; picking three means leaving him out, which is a real cost. Allocation among theory, 2D experiment and 3D experiment is the unresolved question.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently in many materials and techniques; the field is mature and the interpretation is stable. Timing is good, perhaps overdue.
uncertainties: Credited list omits Bernevig, Zhang and Hughes, whose HgTe proposal was important; fair allocation is unclear.
Choosing Molenkamp over Hasan is a judgment on 2D versus 3D experimental priority.
I defer to condensed-matter colleagues on relative importance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle graphene is a clean and tunable platform for correlated insulators and unconventional superconductivity, and it has produced a wave of new experiments. The theory of flat bands at the magic angle combined with the experimental discovery gives a clear story. Originality and impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity, which is the decisive measurement. Andrei's earlier work on Dirac fermion flat bands and twist-induced localisation is a plausible fourth claim, and leaving her out will need to be justified.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups worldwide and extended to other moire systems. Explanation of the superconducting mechanism remains open, so the physics is mature as a platform but not as a settled theory. Timely but somewhat early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism in the superconducting phase is unresolved.
Allocation among Jarillo-Herrero, Andrei and the theory pair is contested.
Sample-to-sample variation (twist angle disorder) complicates reproducibility.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and have opened precision tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. As an instrument builder I value this strongly: it is a measurement technology whose systematics were fought down patiently. The magic-wavelength idea was a clear invention.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice concept and built the first demonstrations; Ye's group pushed the accuracy and stability to record levels. A two-person prize is a clean configuration. Other contributors (Hall, Hansch earlier recognised; ion clock work by Wineland) are outside this entry.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent clocks (Sr, Yb) agree at the 1e-18 level and the work is mature. A redefinition of the second is in preparation, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes (frequency combs 2005, ion control 2012) may weigh on novelty.
Other lattice clock groups (e.g. Lemonde, Le Targat, Ludlow) are not in the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP produced the first high-precision full-sky CMB maps and fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model to percent level, including age, geometry and composition. It is a landmark observational dataset, with careful systematics control. Cosmology has been recognised in 2006, 2011 and 2019, so the question is whether this adds a distinct discovery.
assessment.attribution: Bennett was the PI, Page was a leading instrument and experimental scientist, and Spergel was the leading analyst for cosmological parameters. This is a reasonable three-person configuration, though it ignores the large team and Planck, a successor with better precision.
assessment.maturity: Results confirmed and refined by Planck and ground-based experiments, so confirmation is excellent and interpretation stable. Recognition is somewhat late, and the prize may be seen as covered by COBE.
uncertainties: The incremental step relative to COBE and relative to Planck may be judged insufficiently distinct.
Large team credit to a three-person list; Planck leadership is not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED is the architecture behind superconducting quantum processors: strong coupling of a superconducting artificial atom to a microwave resonator, with dispersive readout and control. The impact on quantum technology is very large. In 2025 the prize went to superconducting circuit tunnelling, so the committee must consider overlap and sequencing; I defer to colleagues on quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Blais (theory proposal with Wallraff, Schoelkopf and others), Wallraff and Schoelkopf (first experiments, 2004) are the central names. Credit to Girvin, Huang and Majer and the transmon work of Koch et al. is not in the supplied list and may be required for a fair prize.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation across many laboratories and platforms; the approach is mature. Timing is good because of quantum computing, but the 2025 prize reduces the chance of an adjacent award soon.
uncertainties: Recent 2025 prize in a neighbouring area; overlap and timing.
Transmon and other contributors (e.g. Girvin, Devoret group) are outside the credit list.
I defer to colleagues on quantum-circuit physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background opens a new band of the spectrum, found by timing millisecond pulsars to microsecond precision. This is detector-style work I admire: very long baselines of calibration and noise modelling. The impact will be large if the signal is confirmed.
assessment.attribution: The result belongs to NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA and IPTA, with many contributors. The supplied names are leaders of the efforts, but none of them can be said to have a decisive individual claim. The configuration is a weak fit and an unresolved credit problem.
assessment.maturity: Evidence at about 3-4 sigma with Hellings-Downs correlation hints; no individual detection above 5 sigma, and the source (supermassive black-hole binaries versus new physics) is not settled. Premature for a prize at present.
uncertainties: Significance is below the conventional discovery threshold; I am relying on memory of the 2023 announcements.
Collaboration-based credit does not map cleanly to three people.
Origin of the signal is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical readout and coherent control of single defect spins, especially the nitrogen-vacancy centre in diamond, gave nanoscale quantum sensors that work at room temperature. I find the sensor aspect appealing as concrete use of basic research. The field is broad and impactful, from biology to materials metrology.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup demonstrated optical detection of single NV spins; Awschalom's group developed coherent control and the quantum-information framing; Lukin's group brought quantum sensing and many-body applications. Walsworth is a further plausible name. Which discovery is the core is not yet obvious.
assessment.maturity: Mature in basic terms and independently reproduced across many groups; applications still being developed. The discovery is somewhat diffuse, so a prize may be early or require sharper focus.
uncertainties: The prize-worthy core discovery is diffuse across several advances.
Lukin also appears in a neutral-atom entry; separate assignment would be needed.
Credit for the single-spin detection is likely contested (Gruber et al. 1997 and others).
